stem: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.text: Scientists have ideas about yawning but no final answer.
Contagious yawning proves that yawns are caused by germs.
Yawning is a habit that people can easily stop.
Yawning always means that a person needs more oxygen.

passage.title: The Mystery of the Yawn
passage.content: Everyone yawns, from newborn babies to elderly people, and many animals do it too. Yet scientists still cannot agree on why. For a long time, people believed that we yawn because our bodies need more oxygen, but tests have not supported this idea. A more recent theory suggests that a yawn helps to cool the brain: when we breathe in deeply, cooler air and extra blood flow may lower its temperature. This could explain why people yawn more often when they are tired or bored, since the brain may be working less efficiently at those moments. Another puzzling feature is that yawning is contagious. Seeing someone yawn, or even reading about it, can make you do the same. Researchers think this reaction may be linked to empathy, although the evidence is still limited.

explanations.title: El principio o la regla aplicable
explanations.content: La idea principal de un texto es el mensaje que abarca todo el pasaje, no un detalle aislado. Conviene preguntarse qué sostiene el autor de principio a fin.

explanations.title: Resolución paso a paso
explanations.content: El pasaje plantea una pregunta (por qué bostezamos), repasa la teoría del oxígeno, la del enfriamiento del cerebro y el bostezo contagioso, y señala que «scientists still cannot agree». Por eso la idea central es que existen varias hipótesis pero ninguna respuesta definitiva.

explanations.title: Por qué no las otras opciones
explanations.content: La afirmación sobre el oxígeno repite una teoría que el texto dice que las pruebas no respaldaron. La idea de que es un hábito fácil de detener no aparece en ningún punto del pasaje. La explicación de los gérmenes tampoco se menciona: el texto relaciona el bostezo contagioso con la empatía.

stem: Why were many shop owners unhappy at first?

options.text: They feared losing customers because of less parking.
They believed the paint would damage their shops.
They thought bicycles would be too noisy for customers.
They had to close the street for six months.

passage.title: Changes on Maple Street
passage.content: Last spring, the city council of Riverton painted a bike lane along Maple Street. At first, many shop owners were angry. They feared that customers would stop coming because there were fewer parking spaces. Mr. Dawson, who runs a bakery on the corner, even collected signatures against the project. Six months later, however, he admits that he was wrong. "I thought nobody would ride a bike in the rain or in winter," he says, "but plenty of people stop here on their way to work." A recent survey shows that the number of people walking past the shops has grown by almost a fifth, and sales at the bakery have gone up. Not everyone is convinced, though. Some residents still complain that delivery trucks block the new lane. The council has promised to move the loading area to the side street before the end of the year.

explanations.title: El principio o la regla aplicable
explanations.content: Las preguntas de detalle se contestan con información que el texto da de forma directa. Hay que ubicar el motivo exacto que el autor menciona y no sustituirlo por algo que suene razonable.

explanations.title: Resolución paso a paso
explanations.content: El pasaje dice que los dueños «feared that customers would stop coming because there were fewer parking spaces». El miedo a perder clientes por la falta de estacionamiento es el motivo de su enojo.

explanations.title: Por qué no las otras opciones
explanations.content: Que la pintura dañaría los negocios no se menciona. El ruido de las bicicletas tampoco aparece en el texto. Cerrar la calle seis meses mezcla un dato incorrecto: los seis meses se refieren al tiempo transcurrido hasta que el panadero cambió de opinión.

stem: Which sentence best summarizes the passage?

options.text: Aztec rulers preferred cacao money to cacao drinks.
Chocolate changed from an ancient drink into a modern treat.
Spanish explorers invented chocolate when they reached Europe.
Chocolate bars have been popular for thousands of years.

passage.title: From Bitter Drink to Sweet Bar
passage.content: Today chocolate is a popular sweet treat, but its beginnings were very different. Thousands of years ago, peoples of Mesoamerica prepared a drink from roasted cacao beans, water and spices. It was bitter, and it was not meant for everyone: in many communities, it was reserved for important ceremonies and for rulers and warriors. Cacao beans were so valuable that the Aztecs even used them as a kind of money. When Spanish explorers took cacao to Europe in the sixteenth century, people there found the drink too harsh. They began adding sugar and serving it hot, and it quickly became fashionable among the wealthy. Solid chocolate bars, the kind we eat today, only appeared in the nineteenth century, when new machines made it possible to separate the cocoa fat from the powder.

explanations.title: El principio o la regla aplicable
explanations.content: Un buen resumen cubre todo el pasaje, de principio a fin, sin quedarse en un detalle ni afirmar algo que el texto no dice. Se descartan las opciones que solo abarcan una parte o que cambian los hechos.

explanations.title: Resolución paso a paso
explanations.content: El pasaje sigue el recorrido del chocolate: una bebida amarga mesoamericana, su llegada a Europa con azúcar y, siglos después, la barra sólida. Esa transformación de bebida antigua a golosina moderna resume el texto.

explanations.title: Por qué no las otras opciones
explanations.content: Atribuir la invención a los exploradores españoles contradice el texto, que dice que ya se preparaba miles de años antes. La preferencia de los gobernantes aztecas por el dinero de cacao es un detalle inventado. Decir que las barras son populares desde hace miles de años contradice el texto, que las ubica hasta el siglo diecinueve.

stem: Why does the author mention that the first week was hard?

options.text: To show that changing a habit takes some effort
To suggest that alarm clocks are difficult to use
To explain why Valeria stopped the experiment
To prove that Valeria could not sleep without her phone

passage.title: A Phone-Free Bedroom
passage.content: Valeria, a university student, used to check her phone until she fell asleep. In the morning, she felt tired, even after eight hours in bed. A friend suggested a simple experiment: charge the phone in the kitchen for one month and buy an alarm clock. Valeria laughed at the idea, but she accepted the challenge. The first week was hard. She kept reaching for a phone that was not there, and she lay awake for a long time. After ten days, however, she began falling asleep earlier and reading a few pages of a novel instead. By the end of the month, she woke up before her alarm and felt more focused during her morning classes. "I don't think the phone itself was the problem," she says. "It was the habit of never letting my mind rest." Today, Valeria still leaves the phone in the kitchen, although she admits that she breaks the rule on weekends.

explanations.title: El principio o la regla aplicable
explanations.content: Una pregunta de propósito se contesta fijándose en la función de un detalle dentro del texto completo, no solo en su significado literal. Hay que ver qué sucede antes y después.

explanations.title: Resolución paso a paso
explanations.content: La primera semana fue difícil, pero después de diez días Valeria empezó a dormir antes y a leer. El contraste muestra que cambiar un hábito exige esfuerzo al principio.

explanations.title: Por qué no las otras opciones
explanations.content: Valeria no abandonó el experimento: sigue dejando el teléfono en la cocina. Los relojes despertadores no se presentan como difíciles de usar. Decir que no podía dormir sin su teléfono es una exageración, pues solo tardó en conciliar el sueño y después mejoró.

Her phone was too old and needed to be replaced.
Phones can never affect how well people sleep.
Her friend's advice about the alarm clock was wrong.

passage.title: A Phone-Free Bedroom
passage.content: Valeria, a university student, used to check her phone until she fell asleep. In the morning, she felt tired, even after eight hours in bed. A friend suggested a simple experiment: charge the phone in the kitchen for one month and buy an alarm clock. Valeria laughed at the idea, but she accepted the challenge. The first week was hard. She kept reaching for a phone that was not there, and she lay awake for a long time. After ten days, however, she began falling asleep earlier and reading a few pages of a novel instead. By the end of the month, she woke up before her alarm and felt more focused during her morning classes. "I don't think the phone itself was the problem," she says. "It was the habit of never letting my mind rest." Today, Valeria still leaves the phone in the kitchen, although she admits that she breaks the rule on weekends.

explanations.title: El principio o la regla aplicable
explanations.content: Cuando se cita una frase del texto, su significado se interpreta junto con lo que la rodea. Las frases dichas por un personaje a menudo expresan una conclusión que hay que reformular con otras palabras.

explanations.title: Resolución paso a paso
explanations.content: Valeria continúa: «It was the habit of never letting my mind rest». Quiere decir que lo que le afectaba era la costumbre de usar el teléfono hasta dormirse, más que el aparato en sí.

explanations.title: Por qué no las otras opciones
explanations.content: Que el teléfono fuera viejo y necesitara cambiarse no aparece en el texto. La idea de que los teléfonos nunca afectan el sueño es una generalización excesiva que ella no hace, ya que ella misma cambió su rutina. Que el consejo del reloj despertador fuera erróneo contradice que el experimento le funcionó.
